tasks.short: Pull the labour-market figures we use in HR reports.

today.trigger: A HR business partner, the compensation specialist, or the HR Director asks how Noordhaven compares with the market, or the monthly labour-market check comes round again.
steps: Look up CBS and UWV figures for the Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo catchment, plus the current pages of the transport CAO and the warehouse CAO.
Pull open roles, time to hire and offer acceptance from Recruitee, and headcount, absence and flex hours from the Power BI extract of AFAS.
Ask the HR business partners what site managers are seeing: no-shows, counter-offers, agency fill on nights and weekends.
Paste the figures into Excel, note the source and the date, and file the workbook on SharePoint.
drudgery: Downloading the same CBS tables again and matching region codes to the three sites
Hunting one wage scale or allowance in a long CAO PDF
Retyping figures into Excel and checking them against last month's file
Chasing site comments that live in mail threads
today.time_sinks: Most of the 78 hours goes to finding the right table, lining up regions with the warehouses, and explaining why a figure moved after the nightly AFAS refresh.

lenses.faster: The repeated download, the region match and the paste into Excel drop out. The analyst reviews one dated file and the short list of figures that moved.
lenses.autonomous: On the first Monday the agreed CBS, UWV, CAO and internal tables land in a dated SharePoint folder with no reminder. A new PDF or a broken table waits for the analyst.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost Noordhaven would keep a standing comparison for every hard-to-fill role at each site, including night and weekend cover, which today is built only when someone asks.
lenses.joy: Re-downloading tables and fixing region codes is the part nobody will miss. Deciding whether a regional average is fair for a Rotterdam driver yard or a Venlo night shift stays with the analyst.
lenses.options: The same request can show three cuts side by side: own staff, own staff plus inleen, and the CAO scale with and without the shift allowance.
lenses.altitude: The analyst maintains the source list, the region map and the rule for accepting a figure. The fetching runs on a schedule.
reach: The compensation specialist's first comparison of scales with regional figures
The recruiters' view of which roles are hard to fill in Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo
FP&A's split of agency hours versus own hours for the labour-cost forecast

tasks.human_edge: Judging whether the statistic is a fair comparison for that site and shift, and whether a manager's comment is fit to keep.
tasks.pattern_why: Known public tables and the internal extract can be fetched on a schedule, while new PDFs, purchased reports and clashing figures need a person before anyone uses them in a pay or hiring conversation.

in_practice.trigger: First Monday of the month, and any request that names pay, hiring difficulty or agency fill.
steps: A scheduled job pulls the agreed CBS and UWV tables and the current CAO scale file into a dated SharePoint folder.
Recruitee and the nightly AFAS extract fill the internal columns: open roles, time to hire, offer acceptance, flex hours.
A new PDF dropped in the sources folder is turned into rows with the source, the date and the sentence the number came from.
Rows that clash with last month, or that lack a source, are listed for the analyst.
The approved file is written to the labour-market table Power BI already uses.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves any new source and any figure that would change a wage, agency or hiring conclusion before the row is marked usable.
data_needed: Agreed CBS and UWV table ids and the region codes that stand for the three sites
Current version of both CAO scale tables, including shift allowances
Role list used for the comparison: order picker, driver, reach-truck, team lead
Agency rate cards, if the contracts allow them to be stored
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint library 'HR labour market', one row per figure with source, pull date and the name of the person who approved it.

evidence.claim: CBS publishes regional labour statistics as open data that a scheduled job can download.
AFAS Profit can feed HR fields to an external report through GetConnectors, which matches the nightly extract Noordhaven already refreshes into Power BI.
A model can lift a wage figure and its page reference from a CAO PDF into a table. Accuracy on allowances has to be tested on Noordhaven's own PDFs.
Power BI can store a dated external table beside the internal HR extract and refresh it on a schedule.

risks: CBS regions can be a poor match for the real catchment of the Tilburg or Venlo warehouse, so a 'shortage' can be an artefact of the map.
A summary of a CAO page can drop a shift allowance and make Noordhaven look over or under the scale.
Manager comments can contain health or performance details that do not belong in a labour-market file.
Purchased reports often forbid uploading the full text to an external model; the file then has to stay in the tenant.
research_questions: Which labour-market sources does Noordhaven already pay for, and which of the last four answers came from a public table rather than a manager's impression?
Do the three agency contracts allow rate cards to be stored in SharePoint and shown in Power BI?
How often in the past year was last month's figure restated after the AFAS nightly extract was corrected?
Which region codes do HR and finance already accept for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo?

tasks.short: Tell colleagues when a report or definition has changed.

today.trigger: A Power BI report, an AFAS field, or a metric definition changes, or someone asks which report to use.
steps: Work out who is affected: HR business partners, recruiters, payroll, learning and development, site managers, or the works council.
Write a Teams post or a mail that states what changed, which report to open, and the new definition in one sentence.
Update the SharePoint page that lists reports and definitions.
Answer the follow-up questions that arrive over the next week, often one site at a time.
drudgery: Rewriting the same explanation for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo
Looking up who still has access to the old report
Updating a SharePoint page that is already behind the model
Repeating the difference between headcount, FTE and inleen
today.time_sinks: The hours sit in the week after a definition change, especially absence and headcount, because each site has its own habit and the questions come back one by one.

lenses.faster: The audience list, the old-versus-new wording and the first draft of the Teams post are ready when the definition is saved. The analyst edits and sends.
lenses.autonomous: Saving a new version of a measure or a dictionary row opens a draft note and a SharePoint update for the roles that use it. Sending stays on the analyst.
lenses.ambitious: Every report in use would carry one current definition, the same sentence in the dashboard, the SharePoint page and the note to the works council, which today drifts apart within a month.
lenses.joy: Retelling the same change three times is the part that goes. Choosing the sentence that a shift supervisor will read correctly is the part worth keeping.
lenses.options: The draft can be a short Teams note for site managers, a fuller note for HR, and a separate formal note when the works council has to be informed.
lenses.altitude: The analyst keeps the audience list and the rule for which changes need the HR Director or the works council. The notes follow the dictionary.
reach: Payroll's message to managers about a cut-off or a new absence code
Learning and development's note when a mandatory certificate rule changes
The HR business partner's monthly site note, using the same figures the dashboard shows

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which change will be misread on a site, and which one must go to the HR Director and the works council before it is posted.
tasks.pattern_why: The change record, the audience and a plain-language draft can be prepared from the dictionary, and a wrong sentence about absence or pay is costly to walk back, so a person sends it.

in_practice.trigger: A measure, a report or a data-dictionary row is saved with a new version.
steps: The change record stores the field, the old text, the new text, the effective date and the roles who use it.
A draft Teams post and a SharePoint page update are prepared from that record, with the report link.
The analyst edits the wording and either sends it or holds it.
Power BI subscriptions for that report stay on the same audience list.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst sends every note. A change to absence, pay, flex use or the 90-day figure is shown to the HR Director before it goes to site managers or the works council.
data_needed: Audience list per report, including which site managers may see which fields
Current definition text and the report URL
Works council calendar, so a formal note is not posted as a casual Teams message
in_practice.logs_to: Version history of the metric dictionary, plus the sent items of the HR analytics mailbox.

evidence.claim: Power BI can subscribe a fixed audience to a report on a schedule, which covers delivery of the report itself.
SharePoint stores page and file version history, so the old definition remains readable after a change.
A model can draft a short change note from an old-versus-new definition. Whether managers read it has to be tested at Noordhaven.

risks: A note sent before the works council has been informed can damage trust on a definition the OR will later challenge.
Managers may still use a local Excel copy, so the post creates a false sense that everyone moved.
Widening who receives an absence or pay report can go beyond what the works council has agreed under the AVG arrangements.
research_questions: Do site managers act on Teams notes today, or do they only open the Power BI app when an HR business partner sits with them?
Is there a written audience list per report, and has the works council agreed it?
How many definition changes in the last two quarters were followed by a correction because the first note was wrong or incomplete?

tasks.short: Write the specification for a report, dashboard, or metric.

today.trigger: Someone asks for a new dashboard, a new cut of an existing one, or a metric for the North Star and its input measures.
steps: Meet the requester and pin down the decision the report must support, the site, and the deadline.
Write the grain, the filters, the AFAS or Recruitee or Studytube field, the refresh, and who may see it.
Send the spec by mail or save a Word file on SharePoint, then wait for comments.
Amend the spec after payroll, finance or a HR business partner points out a definition clash.
drudgery: Rewriting the same header: grain, filter, source, refresh, audience
Searching old mails for how time to hire or verzuim was defined last time
Translating a vague request ('a report on onboarding') into fields that exist
today.time_sinks: The slow part is the back and forth until HR, payroll and finance mean the same thing by FTE, hire date and absence, which often takes longer than the writing.

lenses.faster: The blank spec is filled from the request and the current dictionary, with the source field suggested from AFAS, Recruitee or Studytube. The meetings that remain are about the decision and the definition.
lenses.autonomous: A request logged in a SharePoint form starts a draft spec. It stays a draft until the analyst and the requester accept it.
lenses.ambitious: Noordhaven would finally have one written definition of 'productive and still here at day 90', used the same way by recruiters, learning and development, and the three sites.
lenses.joy: Rebuilding the spec skeleton by hand is the part that goes. The useful part is forcing a clear decision and a clear audience before anyone builds the visual.
lenses.options: The draft can offer two or three grains, for example employee, contract, or site-month, each with what the figure would include and exclude.
lenses.altitude: The analyst owns the spec template and the list of allowed fields. Each new report reuses them and adds only the decision it serves.
reach: The controller's specification of the monthly FTE bridge
Learning and development's specification of a certificate view for heftruck, VCA and food safety
The recruiters' specification of a Recruitee funnel that matches a hire in AFAS

tasks.human_edge: Choosing the decision the report is for, and refusing a cut that would show one person's absence, pay or health.
tasks.pattern_why: A free-text request becomes a fixed spec with checkable fields, and the build does not start until a person accepts that spec. The judgement is in the acceptance, while the paperwork can be drafted.

in_practice.trigger: A HR colleague submits the report-request form, or a dictionary review finds a metric with no spec.
steps: The form captures the decision, the audience, the needed cut and the date.
A draft spec is completed on the template: grain, filters, source system and field, refresh, exclusions, and the North Star link if there is one.
Fields that do not exist in AFAS, Recruitee or Studytube are marked as gaps.
The analyst and the requester edit the draft. If the report shows absence or pay at a fine grain, the HR Director checks the audience.
The accepted spec is stored with the dictionary row before any Power BI work starts.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst and the requester both accept the spec before it is built. Reports that can identify a person's absence or pay also need the HR Director's check against the arrangement with the works council.
data_needed: The request form and the current metric dictionary
A field catalogue for the AFAS extract, Recruitee and Studytube
The audience rules already agreed with the works council
The working definition of the North Star and of verzuim, if one is already signed off
in_practice.logs_to: The metric dictionary in SharePoint, with the accepted spec, the version and the names of the two people who accepted it.

evidence.claim: Power BI datasets already separate measures, filters and row-level roles, so a spec has a concrete place to land.
AFAS Profit GetConnectors expose named fields, so a spec can point at a field that either exists or is a known gap.
A model can map a plain-language request onto a fixed spec template and flag missing fields. Quality depends on the field catalogue it is given.

risks: A fluent spec can hide a field AFAS does not have, such as a 'productive at day 90' flag, and the gap appears only after the build.
Individual absence or pay inside a spec can widen processing beyond what the works council has agreed.
Two accepted specs can still disagree on FTE if finance is not in the acceptance.
research_questions: Is there already a signed definition of 'productive' at day 90, and where is it stored?
How many report requests in the last two quarters were rebuilt because the first spec used the wrong AFAS field or the wrong hire date?
Does the nightly extract document its fields well enough to name them in a spec without opening AFAS?
Which report audiences has the works council already agreed?

tasks.short: Turn this month's figures into a recommended action.

today.trigger: The monthly HR meeting, a site review, or a request from the HR Director for a view on hiring, absence or early leavers.
steps: Refresh Power BI and export the site cuts for time to hire, offer acceptance, week-one onboarding, 90-day retention and verzuim.
Compare with last month and with the other two sites, and check Recruitee and Studytube when the dashboard is not enough.
Write a short note with two or three suggested actions and send it to the HR business partner or the HR Director.
Walk through the note in the meeting and adjust it for things the figures miss, such as a closed contract at one site.
drudgery: Exporting the same five visuals every month
Rebuilding the month-on-month comparison in Excel
Checking whether a spike is a coding change, a small department, or a real shift on the floor
today.time_sinks: Assembly of the pack is repetitive; the time that matters is spent working out whether the figure is real and what a HR business partner can do before the next roster.

lenses.faster: The month-on-month pack, the site comparison and the first suggested actions are ready after the nightly refresh. The analyst spends the time on the action line and the exceptions.
lenses.autonomous: After the nightly refresh a draft pack is waiting for each site. It is not sent until the analyst releases it.
lenses.ambitious: Every site would get a monthly action on the North Star, with the early-leaver roles and the absence duration classes named, which today happens in depth for one site when a meeting demands it.
lenses.joy: Rebuilding the same comparison workbook is the part that goes. The conversation about what the site can actually change this month stays.
lenses.options: The pack can show the same movement four ways: a site effect, a role effect, a cohort of recent hires, and a coding change in AFAS, so the rival explanations are visible before anyone picks one.
lenses.altitude: The analyst designs the pack and the checks that sit behind the action line, and reviews the line before a HR business partner uses it.
reach: The HR business partner's preparation for the site review
The recruiters' choice of which open role to push this month
The compensation specialist's question of whether a hard-to-fill role sits on the wrong scale point

tasks.human_edge: Choosing the action that fits the CAO, the roster and what that HR business partner can do this month, and dropping a suggestion the figures do not support.
tasks.pattern_why: The pack can be assembled from governed metrics and a fixed set of cuts, and a recommended action only counts once the analyst has accepted it. Local knowledge decides which suggestion is usable.

in_practice.trigger: The nightly AFAS refresh finishes, on the working day before the monthly HR meeting.
steps: Power BI builds the site pack for the North Star inputs: time to hire, offer acceptance, week-one onboarding, 90-day retention, verzuim, and manager satisfaction if a survey exists.
Movements past an agreed threshold are listed, each with the rival cuts: site, role, recent-hire cohort, and data-quality flag.
A short action draft is written for each flagged line, tied to a named owner: recruiter, HR business partner, learning and development, or payroll.
The analyst deletes weak lines, edits the rest, and releases the pack to the HR business partners.
Actions that would change a person's contract, pay or medical follow-up are left out of the pack and handled in the normal process.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst releases the pack. The HR business partner for the site accepts an action before it is treated as the plan. No line recommends a decision about a named employee.
data_needed: Governed definitions of the North Star and the five input metrics
Thresholds for what counts as a movement worth showing
Owner per metric
A data-quality flag from the nightly checks so a coding change is labelled as such
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint list 'HR action packs', with the month, the site, the lines released, and the name of the analyst who released them.

evidence.claim: Power BI can produce a scheduled, filtered view per site from the nightly AFAS extract Noordhaven already runs.
Models can draft a short action note from a table of movements and a fixed list of owners. Whether the action is the right one for a warehouse site is a human check.
Employment uses of AI that rank people or decide terms of work fall under the EU AI Act's employment category and carry heavier duties than a group-level briefing a person reviews.

risks: A fluent action line can send a HR business partner after a coding artefact, or after a department too small to mean anything.
If the pack starts ranking candidates or scoring a named person's absence, it moves toward the EU AI Act employment category and toward special-category data under the AVG.
Site managers will ignore a second pack that contradicts the figures finance uses at month close.
research_questions: Do HR business partners change a vacancy, a roster or an absence follow-up because of a written monthly note today, or only after a meeting?
What share of last quarter's spikes in verzuim or early leaving were later explained by a coding change or a group smaller than ten?
Is there a manager-satisfaction source at all, and is the response count high enough to show by site?
Has the works council agreed that group-level action packs of this kind may be produced from the AFAS extract?

tasks.short: Test that the HR figures match the agreed definitions.

today.trigger: A report is about to go to the HR Director, the works council, payroll or finance, or a user says the dashboard does not match AFAS.
steps: Export the Power BI total and the matching AFAS or Recruitee total for headcount, hires, leavers and absence hours.
Tick differences by hand and ask payroll, a HR administrator or a recruiter which coding is right.
Check that mandatory certificates in Studytube still match the roles that require heftruck, VCA or food safety.
Mail the outcome and patch the report, the extract or the definition.
drudgery: Re-exporting the same totals after every nightly refresh
Ticking rows in Excel to find one mis-coded leaver or one pregnancy leave counted as sickness
Asking three people which headcount finance will use at month close
today.time_sinks: The hours concentrate on exceptions and on waiting for payroll or a recruiter to explain a difference, then on re-checking after the next refresh.

lenses.faster: The standard comparisons run after the nightly refresh and only the failed rows are waiting in the morning. The hand export and the full re-tick disappear.
lenses.autonomous: The checks start when the nightly extract finishes. A pass is logged. A fail waits for the analyst, and the report is held if the fail touches a figure that is about to be sent.
lenses.ambitious: Every metric in the dictionary, including the 90-day North Star, would be checked every night, and the works council could see the same pass or fail list that management sees.
lenses.joy: Ticking a long export by hand is the part nobody will miss. Settling a real exception with payroll, and deciding whether the definition itself should change, stays.
lenses.options: A failed headcount can be shown under three agreed rules: contracts active on the last day, average FTE over the month, and own staff excluding inleen.
lenses.altitude: The analyst writes the checks and the exception rules, reviews the fails, and changes a rule only when payroll, finance and HR accept the new definition.
reach: Payroll's tie-out of absence hours before the monthly payroll close
The controller's headcount and FTE tie-out to the general ledger
The check that agency hours billed match hours ordered, which today sits between HR and the bookkeepers

tasks.human_edge: Ruling on the exception: a rehire, a pregnancy leave coded as sickness, a contract change, or an agency worker who appears as own staff.
tasks.pattern_why: The comparisons are rules over structured fields, the output is a pass or a named exception, and a model is not required to run them. A person still decides new rules and odd cases.

in_practice.trigger: The nightly AFAS extract finishes, and again before any pack is sent to the works council or to finance.
steps: A scheduled check compares Power BI headcount with AFAS contracts on the agreed status list, and lists the differing employee numbers for the analyst.
Absence hours are recomputed with the agreed exclusions, including pregnancy leave and people past 104 weeks, and compared with the payroll figure.
Recruitee records in the hired stage are matched to new AFAS contracts, with unmatched rows listed.
Studytube certificates for heftruck, VCA and food safety are compared with the role-to-certificate map.
Inleen hours stay in a separate total. A failed check blocks release of the affected figure.
in_practice.human_gate: Passes need no click. The analyst handles every fail before the affected figure is released, and agrees any change to the rule with payroll or the HR Director.
data_needed: Status list that counts as an active contract, agreed with finance
Verzuim formula and its exclusions
Recruitee stage that counts as a hire
Role-to-certificate map
Rule that agency workers are not in own-staff headcount
Time the nightly refresh is expected to finish
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint list 'HR data checks' with the check name, the date, pass or fail, the count of exceptions, and who closed each fail. Power BI refresh history sits beside it.

evidence.claim: Power BI records whether a scheduled refresh succeeded, which covers the first check: did last night's model update at all.
AFAS Profit stores contract status, absence and payroll results as structured fields that a query can reconcile to a report total.
A small SQL or Python check, written with coding assistance and run on the nightly extract, can list unmatched hires and certificate gaps. This is ordinary engineering, still to be built here.

risks: A check on the wrong status list will certify a figure finance will reject at month close.
Employee numbers in the fail list are personal data and need the same audience limits as the dashboard, under the AVG and the arrangement with the works council.
Certificate rules differ by site. A food-safety check applied to a site that does not handle food will create noise and train people to ignore fails.
research_questions: What is the current gap, in people and in absence hours, between Power BI and AFAS on a normal Monday morning?
Are the verzuim exclusions (pregnancy leave, 104 weeks, partial return) written down and accepted by payroll?
Who is allowed to see an exception list that contains employee numbers?
Does a role-to-certificate map exist for heftruck, VCA and food safety, and is it the same at all three sites?

tasks.short: Compare our hiring and pay with the regional labour market.

today.trigger: A role stays open, agency use rises at a site, or the compensation specialist starts a look at scales, allowances or the flex margin.
steps: Pull Noordhaven's time to hire, offer acceptance, starter pay and leaver reasons from Recruitee, AFAS and Power BI.
Set those beside CAO scales, CBS and UWV regional figures, and the agency fill and rates from the three portals.
Read the few sector notes and vacancy ads the recruiter has saved, and sketch what competitors seem to be paying for the same role.
Write a short comparison for the compensation specialist and the recruiters.
drudgery: Rebuilding the role-by-site table each time a comparison is requested
Stripping advertised rates out of vacancy texts by hand
Separating base pay from shift allowance so the comparison is not misleading
today.time_sinks: The slow part is making pay comparable: full-time equivalent, age or scale step, shift allowance, and the difference between the transport CAO and the warehouse CAO.

lenses.faster: The internal columns and the public CAO and regional columns are filled on a schedule. The analyst works on the mix and on the short comment.
lenses.autonomous: A monthly comparison table is produced for the hard-to-fill roles. The comment is released only after the analyst accepts it.
lenses.ambitious: Noordhaven would see, every month and for each site, where it is losing candidates and where the agency margin has replaced a permanent hire, which today is assembled for one role when the pain is already obvious.
lenses.joy: Rebuilding the comparison grid by hand is the part that goes. Reading whether a gap is a real hiring problem or a mix of age, shifts and allowances stays, and it is the interesting part.
lenses.options: The table can show five views of the same role: base scale, scale plus shift allowance, advertised rate, agency hourly cost, and time to hire against the regional tension figure.
lenses.altitude: The analyst keeps the comparison definition and the role map, and reviews the monthly table. The compensation specialist still owns any proposal to change pay.
reach: The compensation specialist's scale review under both CAOs
The recruiters' pay line in an offer conversation
FP&A's labour-cost forecast, with agency margin shown separately from own-staff pay

tasks.human_edge: Seeing whether a gap against the scale is a mix effect or a real reason candidates go elsewhere, and leaving the pay proposal with the compensation specialist and the HR Director.
tasks.pattern_why: Vacancy text and sector notes are unstructured, the internal and CAO figures are structured, and both can be turned into one checkable table. The comment on what to do about pay stays gated because it can become a proposal.

in_practice.trigger: The monthly labour-market file is approved, or a role passes its time-to-hire threshold.
steps: Internal figures are lined up by role and site: time to hire, offer acceptance, scale point of recent starters, leaver rate before day 90, and inleen hours.
CAO scale points and the agreed regional figures are placed on the same rows.
Vacancy texts and sector notes dropped in the sources folder are reduced to a rate, a location and a date, each with the sentence it came from.
Rows where base pay and shift allowance cannot be separated are flagged.
The analyst writes or edits the comment and releases the table to the compensation specialist and the recruiters.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst releases the table. Any sentence that proposes a pay change, a different allowance or a different agency mix is marked as a draft for the compensation specialist and the HR Director. The works council is informed where the pay rules require it.
data_needed: Role map that lines up AFAS job titles, Recruitee vacancies and CAO scales
Starter pay and allowances from AFAS, at the grain the AVG arrangement allows
Agency hourly cost, if the contract allows it to be stored
Regional tension or vacancy figures and the region map
Time-to-hire threshold that flags a role
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint library 'Pay and market comparison', with the month, the sources, and who released the table.

evidence.claim: CBS and UWV publish regional labour-market figures that can be set beside an internal hiring table.
AFAS Profit holds contract scale, allowances and hours, so a like-for-like pay comparison is possible from the existing extract if the fields are included.
A model can pull a stated hourly rate and location from a vacancy text into a row with a source sentence. Competitor base pay is often absent from public ads, so the row will often be empty.

risks: Public vacancy ads rarely show the full pay, so a comparison can look more precise than the sources allow.
Putting individual starter pay into an external model, or into a report the recruiters forward, can breach the AVG and the pay-confidentiality expectations of the CAO.
A pay comment that reaches site managers before the compensation specialist and, where required, the works council, will be treated as a promise.
research_questions: For the roles that stayed open longest last year, did Noordhaven have any source other than the CAO scale and the recruiter's impression of competitor pay?
Are starter scale, allowances and hours present in the nightly AFAS extract, or only inside payroll screens?
Do the agency contracts permit storing the charged hourly rate next to the CAO scale?
Which pay comparisons, if any, already require works council involvement under the current regulations?

tasks.short: Prepare the employment reports HR and the works council need.

today.trigger: The monthly HR cycle, the payroll close, a works council meeting, or a deadline under the Wet verbetering poortwachter.
steps: After payroll has updated absence, refresh Power BI and export headcount, FTE, in- and uitstroom, verzuim and flex use by site.
Build the workforce cut the works council receives, and the headcount bridge the controller expects.
List employees approaching a poortwachter date so HR administration can act, without copying medical notes.
Save the pack on SharePoint and mail the links, then correct the figures people challenge.
drudgery: Rebuilding the same monthly tables and the FTE bridge in Excel
Separating pregnancy leave and long-term disability from sickness so the verzuim rate is usable
Reconciling HR headcount with the figure finance will put next to labour cost
today.time_sinks: The time goes into definition clashes at month close and into rebuilding packs that differ only by site, CAO and fixed versus flex.

lenses.faster: The standard monthly pack is produced from the nightly extract and the accepted definitions as soon as payroll's absence entries are in. The analyst reviews exceptions and releases it.
lenses.autonomous: The pack runs on the payroll calendar. It waits for release when a check has failed or when the works council version is due.
lenses.ambitious: The same definitions would feed the works council, the insurer's absence pack, the controller's FTE bridge and the poortwachter timetable, every month, with a certificate-compliance page added for the roles that need one.
lenses.joy: Rebuilding the monthly workbook is the part that goes. Signing off a pack that the works council and finance will both recognise is the part the analyst keeps.
lenses.options: Each pack can be issued as own staff, own staff plus inleen, and FTE versus heads, so the works council and finance can see the cut they asked for from the same source.
lenses.altitude: The analyst maintains the report calendar and the definitions behind it, and reviews the release. The generation of the standard pages leaves the desk.
reach: HR administration's timetable of week-6, week-8, week-42 and first-year poortwachter dates
The controller's monthly FTE bridge
Learning and development's list of expired heftruck, VCA and food-safety certificates

tasks.human_edge: Releasing a pack that goes outside HR, keeping health details out of it, and standing behind the definition when the works council or finance challenges a figure.
tasks.pattern_why: These reports follow written definitions over structured HR fields, so they can be produced and checked without a model. A short cover note can be drafted and still needs a person before it is sent.

in_practice.trigger: Payroll marks the monthly absence update complete, and the works council calendar marks a reporting date.
steps: The standard pages refresh: headcount and FTE by site and CAO, in- and uitstroom, verzuim by duration class, inleen hours, and the 90-day retention figure.
A separate list shows employees crossing the poortwachter dates HR administration tracks, with no diagnosis and no medical text.
Certificate gaps for roles that require heftruck, VCA or food safety are attached as their own page.
Failed data checks hold the affected page. The analyst clears or explains each hold.
The analyst releases the internal pack, the finance bridge and the works council pack as separate audiences.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst releases each audience's pack. The HR Director sees the works council pack before it is sent. HR administration owns the poortwachter file and the contact with the employee and the bedrijfsarts.
data_needed: Definitions of headcount, FTE, hire, leaver, verzuim and inleen, agreed with finance and payroll
Poortwachter date rules and the HR administrator who receives the list
Works council reporting calendar and the fields that pack may contain
Role-to-certificate map
Payroll close timestamp
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint list 'HR statutory and OR packs' with the period, the audience, the definition version, the check result, and who released it.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit already produces HR, absence and payroll reports from the same contract and absence records the nightly extract uses.
Power BI can publish one dataset to different audiences with row-level security, which is the practical way to separate the works council pack from a finance bridge.

The EU pay transparency directive covers employers of Noordhaven's size. The exact Dutch reporting fields and first reporting year should be confirmed against the transposed rules before a gender pay page is added.

risks: A verzuim page that includes pregnancy, partial return or people past 104 weeks under the wrong rule will mislead both the insurer conversation and the works council.
The poortwachter list is personal data. Adding medical content would make it special-category data under the AVG and would overlap the bedrijfsarts's file.
An FTE definition that HR releases and finance does not use will double the argument at every month close.
research_questions: Which of these packs does AFAS already produce at a button, and which are rebuilt in Excel only because the definition is local?
What workforce figures does the works council already receive, and which fields are still in dispute?
Who receives the poortwachter date list today, and does any copy of it contain medical text that a report must leave out?
Has finance signed the FTE definition, including part-time contracts and people on multiple contracts?

tasks.short: Keep the metric dictionary and report templates up to date.

today.trigger: A definition changes, a template is copied and starts to diverge, or someone cannot find the current version of a report or a measure.
steps: Search SharePoint and the Power BI workspace for the current dictionary, the report template and the request form.
Update the definition, the owner and the source field, and archive the copy that is no longer current.
Tell the people who keep their own version: payroll for absence, recruiters for funnel stages, learning and development for certificates.
Chase the review that was due last quarter and never happened.
drudgery: Hunting 'final' and 'final v2' files
Copying one definition into the dictionary, the dashboard tooltip and the works council note
Reminding owners whose review date has passed
today.time_sinks: The hours go to finding which copy is current and to chasing owners, more than to writing the definition itself.

lenses.faster: The current file, the owner and the review date are already on the record. A changed measure proposes the dictionary update, and the search for the latest copy disappears.
lenses.autonomous: A review date, or a saved change to a measure, opens a proposed update. The old text stays in force until the analyst accepts the new one.
lenses.ambitious: Noordhaven would have one library for the North Star, the absence definition, the FTE bridge and the certificate rules, and private Excel definitions in payroll, recruitment and finance would lapse.
lenses.joy: Hunting for the latest file is the part nobody will miss. Writing a definition that a site manager and the works council will both accept is the part worth keeping.
lenses.options: A proposed change can be stored as three wordings: the precise rule for the dictionary, the sentence for the dashboard, and the sentence for the works council.
lenses.altitude: The analyst sets the required fields and the review calendar for the library, and approves changes. Keeping the files in line becomes the system.
reach: Payroll's written rule for what counts as verzuim
The recruiters' definition of the Recruitee stages that count as an offer and a hire
Learning and development's rule for which roles require heftruck, VCA or food safety

tasks.human_edge: Deciding that a definition has really changed, and getting payroll, the HR business partners and the works council onto that one version.
tasks.pattern_why: The library rules, the review dates and the link to a changed measure can run without a model, and replacing a definition is the point where a person has to agree, because every report copies it.

in_practice.trigger: A measure changes in Power BI, a spec is accepted, or a dictionary review date falls due.
steps: Each asset has an owner, a review date, a source field, a version and the audiences that use it.
A change proposes a new version with the old text kept beside it and the reports that still use the old text listed.
The three wordings (rule, dashboard sentence, works council sentence) are drafted for the analyst to edit.
The analyst accepts the new version or sends it back. Acceptance retires the old file from the current folder.
Overdue reviews are listed each Monday until the owner confirms or the analyst escalates them.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst accepts every replacement of a definition. A change to verzuim, pay, FTE or the 90-day figure also needs the named owner, and the HR Director when the works council uses that figure.
data_needed: The list of current reports and measures, and who owns each
The field catalogue and the accepted specs
Review calendar
Audience list per definition
in_practice.logs_to: Version history on the SharePoint dictionary, including who accepted the version and which reports still pointed at the previous one.

evidence.claim: SharePoint version history and a required-column library can hold one current definition and keep the previous versions readable.
Power BI measures can carry a description, so the dashboard text and the dictionary can be checked for drift.
A scheduled comparison can list reports whose displayed definition differs from the dictionary. The organisational fact of whether owners will give up their private files is unproven here.

risks: A clean library that nobody opens will sit beside the Excel files people actually use.
Replacing a verzuim or FTE definition without payroll and finance will make the monthly packs look newly wrong.
Templates that include example employee rows can spread personal data into a library with a wider audience than the dashboard.
research_questions: How many competing definitions of verzuim, FTE and a 'hire' exist today, and who owns each?
When a definition last changed, did recruiters, payroll and the works council pack all move, or only the dashboard?
Is SharePoint the place HR actually looks, or do the working copies live in mail and local Excel?
Are example rows in current templates real employee data?

role.altitude: Owner of HR's definitions, checks and report calendar. The standard figures for hiring, absence, certificates and headcount are produced on a schedule, and this person designs those rules, releases the exceptions, and improves the set when a site, a CAO change or the works council shows that a rule is wrong.
reach: The controller's monthly FTE and headcount bridge, up to the point where finance checks the money
The compensation specialist's first comparison of pay with the CAO scales and regional figures
The recruiters' Recruitee funnel report: time to hire, offer acceptance and source of hire
Learning and development's compliance view of expired heftruck, VCA and food-safety certificates
HR administration's timetable of Wet verbetering poortwachter dates, while the conversation with the employee stays with HR administration, the manager and the bedrijfsarts
The standard monthly site pack a HR business partner now assembles by hand, while the meeting with the site manager stays with the HR business partner
role.ceiling_note: This is one FTE at EUR 78 an hour. These eight tasks are about 540 of the role's 1,600 hours, a bit over a third of the year and about EUR 42,000 of loaded cost. Even a large cut in that time is smaller than a few failed hires or a month of extra inleen, so the ceiling is not analyst hours. It is the nightly AFAS extract, the discipline of Recruitee stages, the works council's agreement on what may be reported, and the AVG limits on employee-level data. Payroll filing, the bedrijfsarts's advice, dismissal and pay decisions, and the HR business partner's relationship with a site stay outside the role.
skills_to_grow: AFAS Profit GetConnectors and the contract, absence and payroll fields behind the nightly extract
Power BI modelling and row-level security for HR audiences
Writing definitions that payroll, finance, site managers and the works council will share
AVG and the works council's role when a personnel-data report changes
Both CAOs well enough to see when a pay or allowance comparison is misleading
Small SQL or Python checks against the extract, written and tested with coding assistance
role.ambitious_version: The analyst runs one governed people-data layer that HR, finance and the works council can all trace to a definition. Every month, each site sees the North Star (a hire who is productive and still here at day 90), the input metrics, the absence duration classes, the flex hours and the certificate gaps, from the same AFAS, Recruitee, Studytube and agency figures, with fails shown rather than smoothed. The analyst's own year goes to the questions that change a vacancy, a roster or a return-to-work path, and to the cases the rules miss: a CAO reclassification, a Venlo night shift, a cohort of agency workers near a contract limit.
